notes.summary: Independent whole-current reconstruction finds no identified gap in the constrained countable closure or bounded continuous uniqueness arguments. New scoped proofs give finite scalar-extension preservation and integrable unbounded defect currents against every fixed bounded curvature test. Full original P16.7 remains open.
notes.detailedSummary: Retain K=C((s)), |s|=exp(-1/8), X=(Gm²)^an/<(s⁸,2),(3,s⁸)>, θ=DD(|x|²/2), and raw mass two. Independently reconstruct the all-stage continuous CLD cone, canonical cubic generated energy, every-presentation actual MA/mixed measures, finite FULL bounded dual, moving moments, comparison and clamps. The constrained diagonal gives exact pointwise countable decreasing closure, including poles, but not net or energy-sublevel compactness. The coordinate-curve argument gives uniqueness only for bounded continuous solutions, with varying-ground-field calibration, signed pushforward, finite Galois averaging, Gauss-ray integration and strict-affinoid density checked separately. New proofs preserve generated energy and products under finite scalar extension and dominate arbitrary compact smooth moment probes by finitely many bounded mixed MA measures. Consequently uθw is coefficient-integrable for every generated u and fixed continuous bounded w, and equal generated MA implies DD(uθw−vθw)=0. No uniform divisor-cap integrability, unbounded divisor restriction, full pointwise uniqueness, separated compactness, envelopes or arbitrary-support existence follows. These are unverified proof drafts under disclosed conventional foundations.
notes.text:
Only unchanged original P16.7 is addressed. There are no incoming correctness grants, and no supplied note, verdict, program or compilation is a theorem premise.

Retained objects are K=C((s)), |s|=exp(−1/8), t=s⁸, Y=(Gm²)^an, Λ=<(t,2),(3,t)>, X=Y/Λ, xi=−log|zi|, ρ=|x|²/2 and θ=DDρ. Integration uses the CLD calibration and raw mass ∫θ²=2. The two-dimensional wedge factor is two; the coordinate tangent lattice is saturated and has multiplicity one. No probability normalization or support restriction is introduced.

The applied conventional foundations are CLD v2 8.1.7–8.1.8 for the entire minimal continuous psh sheaf; 8.5.1 for continuous multiplication of order-zero currents; 8.5.3, 8.5.5 and 8.5.6 for the relevant closed-form, positivity and proper-projection calculus; 8.7.1–8.7.5 and 8.8.1, 8.8.4–8.8.5 for continuous generated products and dpsh extensions; 7.2.8–7.2.11 for Radon/coefficient measures and positive order-zero functionals; 6.2 for cutoffs; and 5.11.1 for compact boundaryless Stokes. Poincare–Lelong is 16.7.3. Proper push commutes with differentiation by 7.7.8. Calibration over K of a space over finite L is [L:K] times calibration over L by 14.4.3. Scalar-extension fundamental push has factor one over varying ground fields by 15.3.1 and 16.1.1. Their actual applied statements and immediate proofs were read in the frozen literal units. The erroneous arbitrary-multiplier closedness passage at 8.6.7 is not used.

The analytic foundations include Gruson IV.5 Theorem 1, Van der Put rational-domain presentations and coherent gluing, Conrad–Temkin 2.3.1 and 4.2.3–4.2.4, the read Ducros regularity statements, and the specified Stacks function-field/UFD statements. Deeper Tate/Weierstrass, Kiehl, regular-local algebra, Gruson’s cited inputs and Thuillier/semistable foundations remain named conventional dependencies, not newly recursively proved. Compact-Hausdorff Riesz representation and the elementary distributional affine-function theorem are also disclosed conventional foundations. Exact applications and reading qualifications are in the local ledger.

Geometry reconstruction. Tropical periods are Z². Boxes of widths less than one give ordinary injective quotient charts. The compact polyannulus over [0,1]² surjects onto X. Only finitely many closed deck graphs meet bounded boxes. Closed-relation descent uses a finite flat quasi-finite atlas and its product, never the infinite-sheeted map Y→X. Thus X is compact Hausdorff, separated, good, strict, smooth, connected, boundaryless and pure of dimension two, hence proper.

For Pm={|s|m≤|zi|≤|s|−m}, line bundles are trivial. To see this, induct on annulus factors in mixed products of discs, circles and annuli. Fill one annulus with its inner disc; the overlap is its inner circle. Trivialize on the overlap, glue to the trivial inner-disc bundle, and restrict a trivial frame from the filled product. The zero-annulus case is Gruson’s SK0=0 determinant consequence. Tate/Kiehl supplies the coherent gluing. A unit b on Pm has affine Gauss log norm because both its norm and the inverse norm are convex. Thus b=bαzα(1+g), with ||g||Pj≤|s|m−j for j<m. Successive frame normalization and convergent products give Pic(Y)=0. Letting m increase also proves that global units on Y are scalar monomials.

A pulled-back line bundle has deck factors c1zh1,c2zh2. Writing h1=(A,B), h2=(C,D), commutation gives tC2D=3AtB, hence C=B and A=D=0. Therefore h1=(0,k), h2=(k,0). If k≠0, take λ=λ1λ2sgn(k) and h=(k sgn(k),k). Then v(λh)=2|k|>0. Equivariance imposes a(m+jh)=am cj λ−jm−hj(j+1)/2. A nonzero coefficient has valuations tending to minus infinity quadratically, contradicting Laurent convergence on compact polyannuli. If k=0, the two equations allow at most one Laurent exponent; every nonzero section is a nowhere-zero monomial and sections are proportional. A meromorphic function has an invertible pole ideal by regular-local factoriality and flat restriction. Trivializing its pullback to Y gives numerator and pole frame as equivariant sections of the same bundle; their ratio is constant. Hence Γ(X,MX)=K. An algebraization would be smooth integral proper of dimension two, and its transcendence-degree-two function field would inject into this field K. This contradiction gives genuine nonalgebraizability.

Bounded all-stage calculus. Let C be the actual continuous real weights a for which ρ+a belongs locally to the entire minimal continuous generated CLD psh sheaf. Set Ta=θ+DD[a], B(a,b)=θ∧Tb+DD(aTb), and MA(a)=B(a,a). The source calculus gives positive symmetric local mixed measures of mass two. Convex/max closure is proved for smooth generators by convex smoothing and then extended by two-slot minimality and local uniform closure, including every generated stage.

The additional Green argument is independently reconstructed. For fixed positive closed (1,1) T, complete compact smooth one-forms for ∫α∧Jβ∧T. If fj are uniformly bounded smooth psh approximants, χ≤η are cutoffs and ε=||fj−fk||, cutoff Stokes gives
QχT(fj−fk)≤ε²||DDχ∧T||TV/2+2Bε||χ||∞||DDη∧T||TV.
Positivity supplies the local mass bound through ∫ηDD(fjT)=∫fjDDη∧T. This proves strong gradient convergence. Distributional testing gives uniqueness of the gradient. Retain cutoff/Green identities in the constructed class: positive Hessian measures have bounded local masses, continuous multipliers converge uniformly, and the strong Hilbert pairings converge. Consequently this class is a uniform-closed sheaf containing smooth psh functions; minimality includes all generated stages. Partitions and bounded product rules give, for continuous dpsh f,g,
QT(f,g)=−∫fDD(gT)=QT(g,f), and |QT(f,g)|²≤QT(f,f)QT(g,g).
A smooth compact scalar test may occupy either slot.

Define E(a)=⅓∫a[MA(0)+B(a,0)+MA(a)]. Green gives E(0)=0, E(a+c)=E(a)+2c, monotonicity, concavity, derivative ∫(b−a)MA((1−q)a+qb), and second derivative −2QT((b−a),(b−a)). It also gives the cocycle
E(a)−E(b)=⅓∫(a−b)[MA(a)+B(a,b)+MA(b)].
Bounded comparison follows from locality, total mass and max(a,b−ε).

Canonical generated construction. G consists of actual pointwise decreasing continuous C presentations uj↓u with inf E(uj)>−∞. If USC gk↓g<a for continuous a on compact X, the increasing open sets {gk<a} cover X, so a late gk<a globally. Applying this strict compact dominance in both directions to two presentations proves canonical energy, order monotonicity, and finite energy for every presentation of the same generated function. It excludes the identically −∞ limit. Convex combinations and maxima stay generated.

Energy on any finite simplex of bounded presentations is cubic. Values on a finite unisolvent set determine every coefficient, so canonical energy limits give canonical coefficient limits. For bounded v, put Pj(q)=E((1−q)uj+qv), Rj(q)=E(quj). Then ∫vMA(uj)=Pj′(0)+Rj′(1). These bounded moments converge independently of presentation.

The span of C is uniformly dense in C(X). Small periodic tropical perturbations separate different tropical classes. In one fibre, a Laurent polynomial A separates distinct seminorms; on an injective box, max(ρa,δ+ε(log|A|−b))−ρa, glued by zero on a boundary collar, is a continuous generated weight separating them. It is zero near zeros of A. The span is a vector lattice because max(c(p−q),c(r−s))=2c max((p+s)/2,(r+q)/2)−c(q+s). For any continuous target F, interpolate its values at each pair of points using separation and constants; finite maxima give global lower approximations agreeing at one point, and a finite minimum gives a uniform approximation. Thus common mass two extends moment convergence to every continuous test. Riesz gives the actual Radon MA(u); polarization gives positive canonical mixed B(u,v). This works for EVERY continuous decreasing presentation, not a selected subsequence.

The FULL bounded dual is E*(μ)=supa∈C(E(a)−∫aμ), for positive Radon μ of mass two. For u≤0 generated, ∫−uμ≤E*(μ)−E(u). Hence finite dual gives integrability, null poles and presentation L1 convergence. Crucially, self-integrability is not assumed: Du=lim∫ujMA(uj) is a finite cubic coefficient, and bounded tangency first proves E*(MA(u))≤E(u)−Du. Only then is the integrability inequality applied. The bounded cocycle gives, for k≥j,
0≤∫(uj−uk)MA(uk)≤3(E(uj)−E(uk)).
Let k and then j tend to infinity; this identifies Du=∫uMA(u), and E*(MA(u))=E(u)−∫uMA(u). If u≤0 and E(u)≥−C, then E*(MA(u))≤2C.

Multivariate cubic interpolation first proves bounded-test variation, then decreases the test to a generated one using finite dual, and finally treats simultaneous generated decreasing families. With generated limits and energy convergence it proves actual weak MA convergence, ∫ujMA(vj)→∫uMA(v), and the fixed-u version ∫uMA(vj)→∫uMA(v). Subtraction gives moving L1. Polarization gives mixed moments and B(a,b)≤2MA((a+b)/2). These steps do not test weak convergence directly against an unbounded function.

For comparison/locality, replace moving differences in bounded Lipschitz tests by the limit using moving L1; then replace the limit by fixed continuous presentations, use weak convergence at that fixed index, and finally let it increase. Indicator ramps work at atom-free levels; only countably many levels are bad. This gives MA(v){u<v}≤MA(u){u<v} and 1{u>v}MA(max(u,v))=1{u>v}MA(u), including actual Borel sets which need not be open. For uA=max(u,−A), the exact restriction is on u>−A, excluding the entire contact set. Discarded mass is at most 3C/A. Mixed discarded mass is at most 2(2Cu+Cv)/A+2(Cu+2Cv)/B. Discontinuous clamps are generated products, not silently continuous CLD products.

Constrained countable closure. Suppose uk∈G decreases with L=inf E(uk)>−∞. Choose continuous presentations fk,j↓uk and enumerate ALL their terms hm, so inf hm=inf uk=u pointwise. Let εn=2−n and rn=Σℓ>n εℓ=2−n. Choose kn≥max(n,kn−1) so ukn<hm+εn globally for m≤n; strict compact dominance gives these finitely many bounds. Choose an inner vn=fkn,jn satisfying those bounds and vn<vn−1+εn globally. This additional bound is available because ukn≤ukn−1≤vn−1. Then an=vn+rn decreases since εn+rn=rn−1. It dominates u and is eventually below each hm+εn+rn, so inf an=u exactly, including poles. Its energy is at least L. Thus u∈G. Comparing the outer sequence to any continuous presentation of u plus ε proves E(uk)↓E(u). Ordered operator/moving-L1 continuity now follows with generated limits actually proved. Countable directed infima and summable nonpositive convex series follow. This is not arbitrary-net cofinality or separated sublevel compactness.

All-test estimate. For bounded a,b,w, let f=a−b, g=(a+b)/2, h=w−g and I=∫(a−b)(MA(b)−MA(a)). Green gives I=QTa(f)+QTb(f)≥0 and QT w(f)−QT g(f)=QTa(f,h)−QTb(f,h). Normalize the functions to be nonpositive and their energies ≥−C. Finite dual bounds each absolute MA moment by 3C and each mixed moment by 6C. Since |h|≤−w+(−a−b)/2, each QTa(h), QTb(h) is at most 12C+3C+6C=21C. Therefore
QT w(f)≤I/2+sqrt(42CI).
For equal generated MA measures, moving moments give I(uj,vj)→0, hence QT w(uj−vj)→0 for EVERY fixed w∈C. Degeneracy of θ on residue bidiscs prevents inferring constancy from Qθ alone.

Independent bounded uniqueness audit. If a,b∈C have equal MA, d=a−b is continuous and DD(dTw)=0 for every bounded test. For Laurent A, smooth convex caps ψN=χ(log|A|+N), zero below the cutoff and affine above it, are smooth even at A=0. Glued cap weights give DD(dDDψN)=0 on an inner box. Poincare–Lelong gives positive-current convergence to δdiv A, and CLD 8.5.1 permits the continuous multiplier d. Thus DD(dδdiv A)=0. For every local holomorphic F, rational-domain Tate-series truncation and controlled Laurent approximation give Fn=An/Qn→F, with unit denominators. On compact full-dimensional test supports avoiding F=0, |Fn|=|F| eventually. Poincare–Lelong and continuous multiplication extend the identity to all local principal holomorphic divisors.

For irreducible P(z1) with nonzero constant term, CP={P(z1)=0} is reduced smooth Gm,L, L=K[z1]/P, and its closed immersion j is proper with multiplicity one. All-stage function pullback gives a continuous dpsh restriction. Projection gives j*DD[d|CP]=0. Push is injective for scalar signed Radon measures on a closed embedded image, so its curve Laplacian is zero. Its K calibration is [L:K] times its L calibration.

For finite Galois E/L, form the Laplacian of the pulled-back FUNCTION upstairs. Normalized fundamental push and projection give zero pushforward; the signed measure is Galois invariant. Fibres are single Galois orbits: H(x)⊗LE is a finite etale product of complete fields; a proper union of factor orbits would produce an invariant idempotent, whereas the invariants are H(x). Each factor has its unique extended valuation. Averaging compact continuous tests over the finite group descends them to the proper quotient, so invariant signed measures with zero push are zero. This is not arbitrary-current pullback or infinite extension.

On Gm,E, torus calibration makes H0(q)=h(η0,exp(−q)) satisfy ∫H0φ″=0 on R; it is affine, hence constant by boundedness. On 0<r<|a|, the translated Gauss ray has the same property on a halfline. Continuity as r↓0 and r↑|a| identifies h(a) with the central constant. Finite Galois normal closures cover every closed rigid point. Strict rational neighborhoods and the strict Tate Nullstellensatz give rigid density. Thus each vertical coordinate curve has constant defect. The horizontal z2=1 connects their rigid values; continuity makes d constant on Y and X. This establishes bounded CONTINUOUS uniqueness only. It supersedes current400’s older bounded-uniqueness residual without granting unbounded uniqueness.

Classical/Shilov audit. GR v2’s smooth-recognition input is the unnumbered Section 1.2 paragraph. Wanner’s actual continuous equivalence is Corollary 4.8, combining 4.5 and 4.7, with algebraically closed complete nontrivially valued ground field and smooth proper algebraic tested curve. It is not directly a theorem about X. GR 4.2, 6.1 and 6.4 provide the applied maximum, decreasing-closure and upper-control results. Uniform closure can be converted to decreasing closure by a subsequence with errors 2−j and added 3·2−j. Minimality gives recognition of all local ρ+u weights and their generated limits. For a USC local weight q, maximum principle and USC give q(x)=infA∋x maxΓA q on an actual affinoid neighborhood basis, also at poles. Thus ALL varying Shilov boundary values determine the actual weight. Dense-point equality alone does not. Hartogs upper control supplies no lower-tail or representative compactness.

New finite-extension theorem. For finite F/K and π:XF→X, reconstruct the same classes over F using the same quotient atlas, Green calculus and polynomial construction. Smooth pullback and minimality give π*C⊂CF. For bounded a,b, apply same-field proper projection viewing XF over K: its fundamental push has factor [F:K]. Its integration over K is [F:K] times integration over F. Dividing gives π*BF(aπ,bπ)=BK(a,b), including weighted continuous moments. The cubic formula therefore gives EF(aπ)=EK(a). Pull back every continuous presentation and pass to canonical weak mixed limits: uπ∈GF, EF(uπ)=EK(u), and π*BF(uπ,vπ)=BK(u,v). Finite mixed moments pass by ordinary Borel integration and their already-proved integrability. For Galois F/K the upstairs generated products are invariant, first for bounded products and then by weak limits. The orbit-fibre averaging proof above makes invariant signed push injective. Consequently equal generated MA downstairs implies equal actual generated MA upstairs. This asserts no equality of full duals for arbitrary lifted measures, since CF contains additional tests, and uses no infinite extension.

New probe-domination theorem. Fix w∈C. For every compact smooth symmetric (1,1) probe α, there are finitely many pi∈C and ci>0 such that
|α∧Tw|≤Σci B(pi,w)≤Σ2ci MA((pi+w)/2).
To prove it, cover the support by small injective tropical boxes and strict rational neighborhoods, and use compact smooth partitions. On each piece, α is expressed through finitely many analytic unit moments gj with bounded symmetric coefficient matrix. Approximate each gj by Laurent Aj/Qj with unit denominator and uniform error below its positive minimum norm. The ultrametric inequality gives EXACT equality |gj|=|Aj/Qj| throughout the neighborhood. Thus their smooth moment differentials agree. For the finite Laurent list Hℓ of numerators and denominators, choose smooth convex nondecreasing Φℓ, zero below a cutoff, with Φℓ″≥1 on their compact log-norm ranges and affine above. Ψ=ΣΦℓ(log|Hℓ|) is globally smooth psh on the box, including near zeros, and bounded above there. Its Hessian dominates the sum of squares of all these moment gradients.

The elementary matrix bound consequently dominates both αi and −αi by a finite multiple of DDΨ. Shrink the support into ρa<δ/2; choose δ below the tropical boundary-collar value of ρa and ε small enough that δ+ε sup Ψ<ρa there. Then pi=max(ρa,δ+εΨ)−ρa glues by zero, belongs to C, and Tpi=εDDΨ near the support. There Tpi is smooth, so (ciTpi±αi)∧Tw is positive. Outside the support the desired measure is the positive B(pi,w); locality gives the global signed inequalities. Summing proves domination. The antisymmetric part pairs to zero by J symmetry, so the result controls the entire coefficient current. This argument covers arbitrary analytic moment probes, not only reference tropical coordinates.

New unbounded current theorem. Each dominating bounded MA measure has finite FULL dual. The generated integrability inequality therefore proves u∈L1(|α∧Tw|) and ∫|uj−u|d|α∧Tw|→0 for every generated u and EVERY presentation. Poles are null for all these coefficient measures. Since u has a finite upper bound b, the functional α↦∫(b−u)α∧Tw is finite, linear and positive on positive probes. CLD 7.2.9 makes it order zero. Subtract it from bTw to define uTw from the actual function. Presentation convergence is coefficient L1 and weak-current convergence.

If MA(u)=MA(v), let fj=uj−vj. The all-test estimate gives QTw(fj)→0. For every compact smooth scalar φ,
|〈DD(fjTw),φ〉|=|QTw(fj,φ)|≤sqrt(QTw(fj)QTw(φ))→0.
The fixed smooth second factor is finite. Differentiating the coefficient-current limit gives DD(uTw−vTw)=0 for EVERY fixed bounded continuous w. The two products are defined separately; no difference of infinite pole values is used.

The remaining limitation is precise. Divisor caps vary with N, and the domination constants and dual energies above need not stay bounded. Thus no passage to DD((u−v)δD), no unbounded divisor restriction and no pointwise constancy have been proved. If a bounded test MA(w) has an actual atom c at ξ, integrability gives −u(ξ)≤(E*(MA(w))+C)/c for nonpositive E(u)≥−C. No such atoms at every Shilov point are constructed here. Being a component of one finite-dual measure does not itself prove finite full dual for a normalized Dirac measure.

The unchanged original gates remain: an adequate actual variational finite-energy domain/recognition; separated normalized energy-sublevel compactness with lower tails and representatives; actual envelopes/orthogonality or a sufficient replacement; existence for EVERY positive Radon raw-mass-two finite-FULL-bounded-dual measure with arbitrary support, or another explicit noncircular sufficient class justified against the literal criteria; and genuine full unbounded pointwise uniqueness modulo constants. Countable closure, bounded uniqueness and the new fixed-probe identity do not remove these gates. No full original P16.7 solution or analytic counterexample is claimed.
